topic.readerProblem: A B2B marketer, founder or services-firm owner needs to know how to be named when buying committees ask AI assistants for vendors, why long multi-stakeholder cycles change what must be published, and how to check whether they are named.
topic.connection: This is AEOeye's core question for B2B: whether AI engines name a brand when buyers ask. The page uses AEOeye's audit records (recommendation benchmark) and our own page-consolidation experience, and points readers to the free audit that tests three unbranded questions on ChatGPT.

assessment: The page answers on the first screen (answer every question a buying committee asks, on crawlable pages, backed by consistent third-party sources) and then supports it with 6sense, Forrester and G2 survey figures, each flagged as vendor-run and self-reported. It explains why committees need a role-by-role question tree (illustrative prompts are labelled as ours, not survey data), what AI cites (earned-media bias study, review profiles), a six-step playbook and a measurement method that accounts for run-to-run variability. It rests on AEOeye's small self-selected benchmark with its caveat and on our consolidation story. It deliberately does not repeat the old page's unverifiable figures (Forrester 70% of the journey, 94% LLM use, Yext citation shares, 89% single-engine domains), does not promise timelines, and does not claim AEOeye monitors daily.

sources.supports: 2025 B2B Buyer Experience Report: nearly 4,000 responses from buyers across North America, APAC and EMEA; the winning vendor was already on the Day One shortlist 95% of the time. Fetched twice with different prompts and consistent; the site blocks curl (Cloudflare), so the raw HTML could not be checked, and only this figure and the sample size were used.

Forrester press release (21 Jan 2026): genAI searches are the starting point for B2B buyers; typical decision has 13 internal stakeholders and nine external influencers; procurement is a decision-maker in 53% of cycles; buyers validate AI output with trusted sources; providers should make claims that trusted external voices can validate. Confirmed in raw page text (curl).

G2 survey of 1,076 B2B software decision-makers: 51% start research with an AI chatbot more often than Google; 69% chose a different vendor than planned; review sites the #2 shortlist influence; cross-chatbot consistency is a top trust signal and inconsistency a red flag; 45% say review-site citations are the most confidence-inspiring signal; 64% encounter inaccuracies often. Confirmed in raw page text (curl).
AI search engines show a systematic bias toward earned (third-party) media over brand-owned and social content, in contrast to Google's more balanced mix.
GEO paper: adding statistics, quotations and citations to content gave 30-40% relative improvement on the position-adjusted word-count metric on GEO-bench. Confirmed in the PDF text.

2,961 runs by 600 volunteers; under 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list in two responses over 100 runs for ChatGPT and Google's AI; author concludes percent visibility across repeated runs is probably a reasonable measure.

Organization structured data on the home page can help Google understand administrative details and disambiguate the organization in search results; no required properties. Confirmed in raw page text.
